data.title: Will PepsiCo Stock Rise or Fall after Q3 Results?
data.description:
PepsiCo (PEP) is set to report its fiscal third-quarter 2026 results before the market opens on October 8. While a modest earnings beat could lift the shares, investors will focus more on the company’s outlook and the performance of its North American businesses. In particular, Frito-Lay North America remains a key concern as weaker volumes, higher prices, margin pressures, and changing consumer spending patterns have weighed on demand.

Wall Street expects PepsiCo to report adjusted earnings of $2.30 per share, compared with $2.29 in the year-ago quarter. Revenue is expected to rise 3.2% year-over-year to $24.95 billion.

With PEP stock trading near its 52-week low, investors will be watching closely to see whether the earnings report can provide a catalyst for a rebound or add to the pressure on the shares.

data.title: Nike (NKE) Defends Its Dividend as Company Restructures
data.description:
Nike (NKE) is defending its dividend payment as its finance deteriorate and it undertakes a restructuring of its operations meant to cut costs and conserve cash. Currently, Nike pays a quarterly distribution to stockholders of $0.41 per share. That gives the slumping stock a yield of nearly 5%, one of the highest payouts among the 30 constituents in the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

Some analysts have suggested that the sneaker giant could cut its dividend to help conserve cash and give the company money needed to help fund its ongoing turnaround strategy. However, management defended the dividend on their most recent earnings call with analysts and media, saying the distribution is safe for now.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: McDonald’s Stock (MCD) Looks Like a Buy after the Dip
data.description:
McDonald’s (MCD) stock’s current dip looks increasingly attractive, and I see MCD as a Buy. For a mature, low-beta business known for steady cash flow, this kind of sell-off is unusual. MCD rarely offers investors many dramatic entry points, but the setup looks very different after it fell more than 30% from its peak earlier this year.

The recent sell-off reflects real and plausible concerns. Affordability remains the biggest problem for the fast-food bellwether, and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) drugs add a new long-term risk. Still, most of the current pressure looks more cyclical than structural. At the same time, the drop makes MCD much cheaper and pushes the dividend yield higher. NEXT also gives management a clear plan to improve restaurant economics and recover traffic.
data.author: Bernard Zambonin

data.title: Accenture Stock (ACN) Is Recovering, but Q4 Earnings Could Decide What Comes Next
data.description:
Accenture (ACN) stock is recovering and seems to have finally emerged from “falling knife” mode. After falling nearly 60% from its January peak and dipping close to $118 after a disappointing Q3, the Dublin, Ireland-based consulting firm has already recovered nearly 50% from its lows. Accenture’s next test will be crucial — its Q4 earnings, scheduled for October 1 before the opening bell.

Part of the recovery was because the market began to realize it may have overreacted by treating the company as a structural victim of artificial intelligence (AI). Moreover, Consulting, its core business, remains weak. Bookings need to pick up, and FY27 guidance could determine whether this rerating has more room to run.

My thesis is that the recovery can continue, but the upside is no longer as attractive as it was a few months ago. I remain constructive and still see ACN as a Buy, though not quite the Strong Buy it looked like before Q3.

data.title: Caterpillar Stock (CAT) Pullback Could Offer a Strong Entry Point
data.description:
Caterpillar (CAT) stock’s pullback could offer a strong entry point, in my view. This is because the global construction equipment manufacturer is becoming less dependent on any single industrial upswing. Today, shares sit about 23.5% below June’s record high. However, Caterpillar exited Q2 with a record $72 billion backlog, marking a 92% year-over-year increase.

CEO Joe Creed said, “Strong order rates and a growing backlog reflect broadening momentum across all three of our primary segments.” The valuation asks the company to execute strongly ahead, but today’s demand mix looks longer-lived than the market’s old cyclical framing. Thus, my CAT stock forecast is bullish.

data.title: Why Alphabet (GOOGL) Still Looks Attractive despite Its Antitrust Risk
data.description:
Alphabet (GOOGL) still looks attractive because its search business continues to generate strong growth and cash flow despite the antitrust risk. Google remains the dominant search engine, giving Alphabet a powerful core business even as regulators challenge how it maintains that position.

As I’ve discussed in a previous article, any company that becomes a verb in common parlance, like Google, has serious staying power. However, Google’s parent company Alphabet has had a fairly bumpy few years. A federal judge ruled in 2024 that Google violated antitrust law by paying Apple (AAPL) to make it the default search engine, and the case remains under appeal. That creates a real risk for the tech giant, particularly if the final outcome changes how Google distributes Search.

Yet, I feel the major issues were addressed at trial, and the company remains one of the more cost-effective names in the megacap corner of the market. As a result, I’m rather bullish on Alphabet as we await the conclusion.

data.title: Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B) to Earn Nearly $50 Million in Annual Dividends from Lennar Investment
data.description:
Lennar (LEN) just declared a dividend payment of $0.50 a share per quarter, or $2 a year. That’s good news for Berkshire Hathaway (BRK.B), which just took a sizable position in the U.S. homebuilder. Berkshire Hathaway, a diversified holding company, is set to earn $47.4 million in dividend payments over the next year from the more than 23 million Class A shares of Lennar that it now owns.

Lennar is scheduled to pay its next dividend on Oct. 22 of this year to shareholders of record as of Oct. 7. LEN stock has a strong forward dividend yield of 2.45%. For Berkshire Hathaway, Lennar is the latest in a series of stocks that company owns that pay strong annual dividends. Other stocks owned by Berkshire that have hefty dividend yields include Coca-Cola (KO) and Bank of America (BAC).

Berkshire Hathaway will earn nearly $1 billion this year in dividend payments from Coca-Cola alone.

Berkshire Hathaway’s Lennar Stake

Earlier this week, it was disclosed that Berkshire Hathaway has built a 10% stake in Lennar, the second largest U.S. homebuilder. Berkshire bought 2.7 million Class A shares of Lennar over three trading days ended Sept. 21, bringing its position to 23.7 million shares worth $1.80 billion, according to a regulatory filing.

The Omaha-based conglomerate that had been led for 60 years by Warren Buffett also owns 528,000 of Lennar’s Class B shares, which have 10 times the votes of a Class A share. The Class B stock also pays a quarterly dividend of $0.50 per share. When the Class B shares are factored into the equation, Berkshire Hathaway will earn more than $48 million in dividends a year from Lennar.

Berkshire’s Homebuilding Investments

Berkshire Hathaway has a sizable presence in the homebuilding market, having acquired Taylor Morrison Homes earlier this year for $8 billion. Berkshire also owns building material companies, including paint maker Benjamin Moore and Johns Manville, a maker of roof tiles. In 2003, Berkshire bought Clayton Homes, a maker of manufactured and modular homes, for $2 billion.

Berkshire’s new CEO Greg Abel has spent this year deploying some of the company’s $367 billion cash pile. The investment in Lennar was likely not directed by Warren Buffett as the 96-year-old businessman recently stepped down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway’s board of directors. LEN stock rose 6% on news of Berkshire Hathaway’s stake in the company. However, the share price is down 33% over the last 12 months amid a downturn in residential real estate.

Not enough analysts cover Berkshire Hathaway’s stock, so let’s look at the three-month performance of the share price. As one can see in the chart below, BRK.B stock has risen 8% in the last 12 weeks.

data.title: Tobacco Giant Phillip Morris (PM) Raises Dividend 9% as It Ramps Up Shareholder Rewards
data.description:

The latest hike continues the company’s streak of increasing its dividend every year since becoming a public company in 2008. Over the past 18 years, Phillip Morris has raised its dividend a total of 248%, or by a compound annual growth rate of 7.2%.

Phillip Morris continues to prioritize shareholder rewards. Over the last decade, Philip Morris has returned $75 billion back to its shareholders through dividends and also stock buybacks.
